# 📦 Models Guide

Models in Padi Go Framework represent your database entities and business logic layer.

---

## 📋 Model Structure

Padi generates models using a two-tier pattern:

### 1. Base Model (`app/Models/Base/`)
Holds struct definitions, database tags, JSON tags, validation tags, and auto-generated relations:

```go
// Code generated by Padi Generator. DO NOT EDIT.
package base

import (
	"time"
	"github.com/wibiesana/padi_go_core/activerecord"
)

type User struct {
	ID        uint       `db:"id" json:"id"`
	Name      string     `db:"name" json:"name" validate:"required"`
	Email     string     `db:"email" json:"email" validate:"required,email"`
	Password  string     `db:"password" json:"-"`
	Role      string     `db:"role" json:"role"`
	CreatedAt *time.Time `db:"created_at" json:"created_at"`
	UpdatedAt *time.Time `db:"updated_at" json:"updated_at"`
}

func (User) TableName() string {
	return "users"
}

func (User) PrimaryKey() string {
	return "id"
}

func (User) Fillable() []string {
	return []string{"name", "email", "password", "role"}
}

func (User) Relations() map[string]activerecord.Relation {
	return map[string]activerecord.Relation{
		"articles": activerecord.HasMany("articles", "author_id", "id"),
	}
}
```

### 2. Custom Model (`app/Models/`)
Generated once. Never overwritten by the generator:

```go
package models

import (
	base "padi-template/app/Models/Base"
	"github.com/wibiesana/padi_go_core/auth"
)

type User struct {
	base.User
}

// Password helper methods
func (u *User) SetPassword(plainPassword string) error {
	hash, err := auth.HashPassword(plainPassword)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	u.Password = hash
	return nil
}

func (u *User) VerifyPassword(plainPassword string) bool {
	return auth.VerifyPassword(u.Password, plainPassword)
}
```
